as_told.title: Foratu's second hypothesis: infection from a scratch by the being

plain: In Varginha, Brazil, in 1996, a man named Marco Chereze is said to have died of an infection that started with a scratch from the claw of a non-human being. A doctor identified as Dr. Armando, who speaks as having seen the case, tells Michels it was "a very distinct and deliberate scratch" on Chereze's skin, and points to Chereze's autopsy report. Ahmed Foratu, a surgeon at a hospital in the town, also speaks as someone who was there. He presents it as the second of two explanations: that Chereze "contracted the infection from a scratch, from contact with an extraterrestrial being". He credits the idea to a Dr. Jannini and to Italo Venturelli, another witness. Both men are firsthand voices, though they frame it differently: Armando speaks of the scratch as a fact of the body, while Foratu offers it as one hypothesis among others. If true, it would mean a person was physically harmed by a being from elsewhere, and that doctors recorded it.
